name: Indira Gandhi
role: Prime Minister of India (1966-1977, 1980-1984); Congress leader
summary: Gandhi led India as a dominant Congress prime minister who combined a state-led mixed economy and socialist rhetoric (bank nationalisation, privy purse abolition, Garibi Hatao) with strong centralisation, non-alignment tilted toward the Soviet Union, and a secular, plural-nation outlook. She declared the 1975-77 Emergency, ruling with censorship and mass detentions, then lost and regained power; the 42nd Amendment added 'socialist' and 'secular' to the Preamble while curbing courts and adding fundamental duties. Her stated views stress democracy and development, but her record on civil liberties and federal autonomy was authoritarian.

notes: Sources are mostly 1969-72 speeches plus the Emergency-era record; her own post-1975 statements (Emergency defence, 1980s interviews) were not obtained, so Emergency answers rest on the record. Some stated positions conflict with her record (non-violence vs 1971 war; democracy vs Emergency); both noted in rationales. Views on social issues (abortion, same-sex questions, drugs, etc.) were not found and are null.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Wanted the public sector to 'influence and control the pace and direction of investment' and used price controls, while still defending a mixed economy with room for private enterprise.

public-ownership.rationale: Her governments nationalised banks (1969), coal, steel, copper, refining, insurance; she wanted a 'growing and dominant role for the public sector' while keeping a mixed economy.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Her 1970 Finance Bill speech presented taxation as a device for 'distributive justice', aimed at reducing extreme income inequalities and tax avoidance; wealth tax was part of the package.

unions-good.rationale: Called an active trade union movement an essential ingredient of a democratic society and trade unionism an instrument for making freedom of association meaningful; also called for strike moratoria.

property-fundamental.rationale: Said she was not against the right to property but wanted ceilings on it, and her government amended the Constitution when courts struck down land reform and bank nationalisation laws.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Backed licensing curbs and the Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Act; spoke of safeguards against concentration of economic power and putting the rest of private industry under strict regulation.

cut-welfare.rationale: Her programmes (Garibi Hatao, public distribution, Twenty-Point Programme) expanded anti-poverty spending; she never argued that welfare breeds dependency.

state-harmful.rationale: Treated the state as the instrument for development, planning and poverty removal.

decide-locally.rationale: Defended a strong Centre and the Centre's control of main revenues, argued state-autonomy demands were unnecessary; the 42nd Amendment moved more power to the Centre.

more-religion-public.rationale: Held that secularism and religious equality underlie the polity; opposed imposing religion on others.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Said development should be achieved without alienating people from their heritage; her cultural policy rested on Indian tradition.

gradual-change.rationale: Wanted rapid transformation of Indian society through the democratic framework, overriding court objections to land reform and nationalisation.

free-trade.rationale: Defended protection of domestic industry and import restraint at India's stage of development; did not hold that open trade benefits everyone.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Justified 1971 intervention in East Pakistan by citing atrocities against 75 million people, refugees, and saying one cannot annihilate a people and call it internal.

limit-growth.rationale: At Stockholm said the conflict is not between conservation and development, called poverty the greatest polluter and said development is a primary means of improving the environment.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Dedicated the Tarapore Atomic Power Station in 1970 as a dream come true that would increasingly contribute to national power needs.

revolution-justified.rationale: Preferred change through parliament, opposed violent extremism, and spoke of a 'bloody revolution' as no solution; praised Bangladesh's struggle and Gandhi as a 'great revolutionary'.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Said domestic industry could not be exposed to import competition and that high import duties were levied in the interest of domestic production.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Said the public sector should control the pace and direction of investment and occupy key positions; investment plans were channelled into public-sector core industries.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Wanted private enterprise to spread and not be confined to a few families, with the base 'much wider'; favoured ceilings and support for small farmers and small manufacturers.

one-party-rule.rationale: Called democracy, secularism and socialism inseparable, said there is no true socialism without democracy and rejected authoritarian alternatives.

democracy-best.rationale: In 1970-72 said democracy strengthens people and that India gained 'human values' by not choosing a stronger dictatorship; the Emergency (1975-77) cut against this, though she restored elections in 1977.

right-to-secede.rationale: Called a party standing for secession of any part of India a serious matter; crushed the Mizo uprising and later ordered Operation Blue Star.

political-violence-never.rationale: Said she did not think any kind of violence could be justified at any time, though she ordered war in 1971 and supported Bangladesh's freedom struggle.

war-builds-character.rationale: Said 'nothing is so pointless as modern warfare' and that a clean war is no war at all.

separate-church-state.rationale: Insisted a true democrat must be secular; the 42nd Amendment added 'secular' to the Preamble. Indian secularism as she described it meant equal rights and no religious basis for parties.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Said secular equal rights for all citizens were essential and condemned imposing one's beliefs on persons of other religions.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Stressed India's plurality (Muslims, Christians, many languages) and rejected parties based on one religion, race or language.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Her 1970 budget and Garibi Hatao stressed distributive justice and reducing inequalities, not only equal opportunity.

self-interest-moral.rationale: At Stockholm said the over-riding concern with self and the profit motive are the basic cause of the ecological crisis.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Her 42nd Amendment added Fundamental Duties (Part IVA); at Stockholm said the modern individual came to believe he had rights with no corresponding obligations.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Said her deep interest in the 'only earth' was 'not for itself but as a fit home for man', while also urging looking on all creation as a friend.

limit-population.rationale: Ran an officially sponsored family planning programme aiming to cut the birth rate; the Emergency period saw a mass sterilisation drive.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Blamed values of industrial civilisation (reckless efficiency, obsolescence) but said fault lies not in science or technology and insisted on industrialisation for the poor.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Scholars note she was decidedly non-ideological and pragmatic; she criticised critics 'imprisoned in set ideas'.

direct-action.rationale: Said violence by extremist political groups should be resisted and that change should come through discussion and democratic processes.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Defended modernisation of tribal peoples against being kept as 'museum pieces' and rejected arguing progress costs spirituality.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Said there can be no true socialism without democracy and rejected extremes; her socialism was parliamentary.

taxation-theft.rationale: Used taxation explicitly as a fiscal device for distributive justice and revenue for development.

total-state.rationale: Said an authoritarian alternative would solve no long-term problems; criticised totalitarian methods; kept a mixed economy and federal democracy.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Declared that alteration of boundaries or any expansionism was 'totally unacceptable' (though India incorporated Sikkim in 1975).

workplace-democracy.rationale: Workers' participation on boards of the nationalised banks; her government's 42nd Amendment added Article 43A on workers' participation in management.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Argued that cutting public-sector outlay brings unemployment and stagnation; rejected critics who wanted outlays kept down.

national-self-determination.rationale: Backed Bangladesh's struggle ('flame of freedom') and the right of peoples to realise national will, while rejecting secession within India.

class-collaboration.rationale: Backed a mixed economy where private and public industry 'complement' each other and worker participation in management.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Condemned South African apartheid and colour bar and demanded 'one man one vote' in Rhodesia.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Favoured a dominant public sector, planning, price controls and extensive welfare and regulatory functions.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Described equal rights for all citizens regardless of religion, caste or language as the test of democracy; at Stockholm lamented lack of recognition of the equality of man across race and religion.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Said the world can progress 'not by conflict, but only through co-operation'; criticised the cult of competitive efficiency at Stockholm.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The 42nd Amendment added Art. 31D and Part XIVA for laws against anti-national activities by individuals or associations.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Garibi Hatao was the theme of her 1971 campaign; she described a 'relentless battle against poverty' as the aim of policy and a public distribution system to protect weaker sections.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: In 1970 backed the President's call for a moratorium on strikes and lock-outs as a patriotic duty (an appeal, not a ballot law); the Emergency later suspended ordinary rights.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: At Stockholm called it an over-simplification to blame the world's problems on population; said poverty lies in inadequate development and that population control needs education and rising living standards.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Declared the Emergency on 25 June 1975, suspending fundamental rights, censoring the press and detaining thousands of opponents without trial under MISA and related rules.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Said that price controls for basic and essential items could not be dispensed with, and spoke of fair-price shops and a public distribution system.

party-controls-media.rationale: Press censorship was imposed during the Emergency; she also criticised concentration and monopoly in the newspaper industry.

clerical-rule.rationale: Her stated test of a democrat was secularism and equal rights; she rejected religion-based politics.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Said membership of armed camps and subsidiary alliances weakens the self-reliance of nations.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The Twenty-Point economic programme was enforced under Emergency 'discipline' with rights suspended, justified as needed for production and poverty reduction.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Authorised development of nuclear weapons in 1967 and the 1974 Pokhran test; refused to sign the NPT.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Backed ceilings on property and curbs on concentration of wealth; spoke of the Directive Principle that ownership and control should serve the common good.

collective-defense.rationale: Opposed military alliances and blocs, preferring non-alignment.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Ordered the army against the Mizo National Front uprising (1966) and ordered Operation Blue Star (1984) against Sikh separatists.

land-redistribution.rationale: Called land reforms urgent and 'a revolutionary measure', and favoured ceilings on rural and urban property; surplus land to the landless was the stated aim of ceiling laws. Full confiscation of all large estates was not her stated line.

refugee-return.rationale: Insisted that Bangladesh refugees on Indian soil should return once conditions were created; descendants were not addressed.

ban-cartels.rationale: Her government's Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Act and Monopolies Commission targeted concentrations of economic power and restrictive practices.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The 42nd Amendment (1976) barred court challenges to constitutional amendments (Art. 368(4)-(5)); its Statement of Objects says Parliament embodies the will of the people and that will should prevail.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Warned that ecology should not add new conditions in rich nations' trade and political policies to weaker nations' burdens.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Condemned extremist political groups resorting to violence as disruptive and said violence breeds violence.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Pushed abolition of the princes' privy purses and privileges as incompatible with the democratic Constitution.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Condemned colonial domination and the 'power of the big stick'; said the West's prosperity rested on dominating others.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Backed laws against untouchability and equal rights for all citizens.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Said she was not against fundamental rights but her governments amended Part III repeatedly and barred judicial review of amendments.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Held Parliament to be the supreme lawmaker; the 42nd Amendment stressed that legislatures embody the will of the people.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Praised Ashoka's edicts protecting animal life and said one should look on all creation with the eyes of a friend.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Fourth Plan aimed to reduce dependence on foreign aid so that aid need 'disappear by the end of the decade'; welcomed foreign investment only selectively (advanced technology, export projects).

single-official-language.rationale: In 1967 introduced the amendment guaranteeing the use of both Hindi and English as official languages and said she'd never align with a party for one language.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Criticised production of goods 'not really needed', planned obsolescence and a model that gives more place to things than to persons.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Said every small country has equal rights and opposed any infusion of outside military force or abridgement of sovereignty.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Her governments pursued reduced birth rates through family planning and sterilisation incentives, not incentives to have more children.

non-intervention.rationale: Opposed interference in other states' internal affairs in general, but said atrocities against a whole people are not purely internal (Bangladesh).

religious-nation.rationale: Rejected defining the polity by one religion, race or language and stressed religious equality as the basis of the political edifice.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Argued key taxes belong to the Union and that revenue should be shared with States through the Finance Commission to help weaker regions.

defeat-communism.rationale: Pursued peaceful coexistence, signed the 1971 treaty with the Soviet Union and sought coexistence with differing systems.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Described India's path as the democratic, secular, socialist path avoiding political extremes, with a mixed economy and 'socialism understood in a slightly different meaning'.

suppress-opposition.rationale: During the Emergency thousands of opposition leaders and activists were jailed and some organisations banned; she presented it as a response to threats to order and security.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: At Stockholm said the West industrialised on the riches and labour of colonised countries and condemned that exploitation.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Said participation in government at all levels strengthens the people and that authoritarian alternatives would not solve long-term problems.

social-market-economy.rationale: Said the Government stands for a mixed economy with areas for private enterprise and public sector, plus regulation and welfare aims.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Said India works for total disarmament as a goal.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Non-alignment was core policy; said alliances and armed camps weaken self-reliance (though non-alignment 'not neutrality').

racial-franchise.rationale: Insisted any constitution for Rhodesia ensure 'one man one vote' in a multi-racial society (NIBMAR).

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Repeatedly said policy must check concentration of economic power and vested interests, tying it to the democratic and socialist path.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Held that government must lead the battle against poverty through plans and the public sector.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Said India was totally opposed to the infusion of outside military force or any foreign power presence in any area and objected to foreign fleets in the Indian Ocean.

spiritual-nature.rationale: At Stockholm defended spirituality as the enrichment of the spirit and said material progress should come without alienating people from their heritage.

future-generations.rationale: Spoke of the need to prolong humanity's tenancy of the planet and of harms to 'the yet to be born'.

arms-reduction.rationale: Said India stands and works for total disarmament and that even small reductions in armaments would help development.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Called for more equitable sharing and accelerated progress of less developed countries; as NAM leader in the early 1980s focused on developing countries' economic grievances.

farm-price-support.rationale: Said farmers should get a reasonable price for their products, with the government reconciling producers' and consumers' interests.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Authorised the 1974 test and refused the NPT, while calling for total disarmament.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Described the 'radical transformation' in the position of women (marriage laws, property rights, divorce) as an achievement of the 24 years of independence.

women-suffrage.rationale: Said women should be enabled to make a full contribution as individuals; praised women's participation in public life and the freedom struggle.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Her government granted statehood or union-territory status to north-eastern hill regions (Meghalaya, Manipur, Tripura, Arunachal Pradesh) in 1972.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Said India could never align with a party that believed in one religion, one race or one language; secularism was the basis of her politics.

national-resource-control.rationale: Nationalised coal, copper and oil refining and wanted nation-controlled core industries; stressed selectivity towards foreign collaboration.
